assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of political-economy research linking political institutions, state capacity, fiscal policy and development outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini made distinct but complementary theoretical and empirical contributions to the modern field.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has shaped scholarship and policy analysis for decades and its central ideas are well established.
uncertainties: The broad umbrella contains several partially distinct contributions, making a single prize citation difficult to delimit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work transformed understanding of how technology, trade exposure and task change reshape local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a coherent core for the empirical literature on trade shocks and changing labour demand.
assessment.maturity: Its methods and conclusions have been extensively tested, extended and incorporated into debates over trade and adjustment policy.
uncertainties: Separating the effects of trade, automation and other regional shocks remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research has substantially changed measurement and explanation of intergenerational mobility.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman form a clear central group behind the linked data infrastructure and influential mobility findings.
assessment.maturity: The work has already generated broad replication, methodological development and policy-relevant research, though it is comparatively recent.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of place-based mobility patterns and their portability across settings remain unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion provided durable alternatives to narrowly self-interested models of economic behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt supplied a particularly influential formal account, while Falk made major complementary experimental contributions.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested across laboratory, field and organizational settings over a long period.
uncertainties: The scope and stability of social preferences across institutions and cultures remain subjects of active debate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research brought natural capital, exhaustible resources and biodiversity into rigorous intertemporal economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central contributors to the theoretical treatment of sustainability and resource depletion.
assessment.maturity: The framework is longstanding and increasingly consequential for environmental accounting and policy evaluation.
uncertainties: Empirical valuation of biodiversity and translation from theory to operational welfare measures remain difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The field-defining analysis of agglomeration and spatial sorting clarified why cities form, grow and differ in productivity.
assessment.attribution: Glaeser, Puga and Duranton represent an identifiable core spanning theory and empirical urban economics.
assessment.maturity: The literature is mature, widely used and influential in regional and urban policy research.
uncertainties: The ballot's broad scope also encompasses housing and related contributors, so the attribution boundary is not sharp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression made distributional heterogeneity accessible in a simple, general and highly influential econometric framework.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the unmistakable originators of the core contribution.
assessment.maturity: The method has been standard across econometrics and applied economics for decades.
uncertainties: Its exceptional methodological reach may nevertheless be viewed as less unified with a substantive economic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research forcefully reframed the role of investor protection and legal institutions in financial development.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes and Shleifer are central to the empirical legal-origins program.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has had long-lasting influence across finance, corporate governance and development research.
uncertainties: The causal status, measurement choices and universality of legal-origin claims have drawn substantial scholarly criticism.
